requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL record the deployed compositor, plugin, shell, compiler and host versions and source hashes before a comparative native run.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: the report identifies every participating artifact; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Create a frozen architecture baseline manifest.

scenarios.name: architecture-001
scenarios.then: the report identifies every participating artifact

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL assign DOM presentation to Elm, Wayland surface lifetime to the native host, and application-window effects to native authority.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: only native authority mutates the application window; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Publish an ownership table and executable boundary probe.

scenarios.name: architecture-002
scenarios.then: only native authority mutates the application window

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL expose one incoming event stream and one outgoing intent stream with versioned, discriminated envelopes.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: both conform to the recorded schema; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Define the envelope schema and Elm decoders.

scenarios.name: architecture-003
scenarios.when: an intent and its outcome cross the bridge
scenarios.then: both conform to the recorded schema

requirements.ears: IF an envelope is malformed or has an unsupported protocol version, THEN the Elm desktop SHALL reject it without a native effect and record the rejection reason.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: no compositor action occurs and a reason is recorded; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.legacyEvidence: new coverage: bridge decoder and authority negative fixtures
requirements.task: Implement validation at both trust boundaries.

scenarios.name: architecture-004
scenarios.then: no compositor action occurs and a reason is recorded

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL attach request identity, compositor lifetime, frontend epoch, operation generation, window incarnation, output generation and expected native revision to window-effect intents.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: the serialized request contains the full authority tuple; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Implement identity-bearing effect messages.

scenarios.name: architecture-005
scenarios.then: the serialized request contains the full authority tuple

requirements.ears: IF an intent identity or expected revision differs from current native authority, THEN the Elm desktop SHALL refuse the intent before mutation.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: the new window remains unchanged; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Add effect-boundary freshness guards.

scenarios.name: architecture-006
scenarios.then: the new window remains unchanged

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL correlate each outcome with its request and represent Pending, Committed, Refused, Cancelled and Unknown as distinct states.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: its state is Unknown rather than Committed; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Implement receipt state transitions.

scenarios.name: architecture-007
scenarios.when: its final effect cannot be proven
scenarios.then: its state is Unknown rather than Committed

requirements.ears: WHEN a dependent effect is requested, the Elm desktop SHALL dispatch it only after the prerequisite receipt satisfies its declared precondition.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: focus is withheld until the required receipt; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Implement an acknowledged dependency scheduler.

scenarios.name: architecture-008
scenarios.then: focus is withheld until the required receipt

requirements.ears: WHEN a duplicate request is received within a frontend epoch, the Elm desktop SHALL return the existing request disposition without executing the effect again.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: only one mutation is recorded; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Implement bounded request deduplication with explicit expired-ID refusal.

scenarios.name: architecture-009
scenarios.then: only one mutation is recorded

requirements.ears: WHEN a snapshot is installed, the Elm desktop SHALL apply only ordered events after its native sequence watermark and request reconciliation on a sequence gap.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: 9 is discarded and the gap before 12 triggers reconciliation; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Implement snapshot and delta sequencing.

scenarios.name: architecture-010
scenarios.then: 9 is discarded and the gap before 12 triggers reconciliation

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL capture modifier press, repeat, release and Escape in native order with chord generation and ordinal before frontend readiness.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: the ready view receives the release in its original chord order; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Retain native chord acquisition and replay it to Elm.

scenarios.name: architecture-011
scenarios.then: the ready view receives the release in its original chord order

requirements.ears: WHEN cancellation reaches native authority before an effect commits, the Elm desktop SHALL prevent that effect and retire its request-owned resources.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: restore is absent and owned helpers retire; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Implement cancellation checks at the final native effect boundary.

scenarios.name: architecture-012
scenarios.then: restore is absent and owned helpers retire

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL retain each original acceptance deadline through retries, queueing, reconciliation and frontend restart.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: the deadline remains unchanged; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Carry immutable absolute deadlines through request state.

scenarios.name: architecture-013
scenarios.given: a request nearing its original deadline
scenarios.then: the deadline remains unchanged

requirements.ears: IF an effect outcome is Unknown, THEN the Elm desktop SHALL reconcile native state before permitting a retry of that effect.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: native truth is read before another mutation; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Implement uncertain-effect recovery.

scenarios.name: architecture-014
scenarios.then: native truth is read before another mutation

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL enforce configured byte and item bounds on bridge queues, coalesce replaceable observations, and reject new effect work explicitly when admission fails.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: memory remains bounded and effect refusal is explicit; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Define queue bounds and test admission saturation.

scenarios.name: architecture-015
scenarios.then: memory remains bounded and effect refusal is explicit

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL reserve bounded control capacity for cancellation, receipts and retirement independently of preview work.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: it uses reserved control capacity and is processed; failure injection and artifact hashes included.

scenarios.name: architecture-016
scenarios.then: it uses reserved control capacity and is processed

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL use one canonical owner for cross-output snap, pin and switcher transactions and send read-only projections to display views.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: one authority serializes the transaction; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Implement canonical multi-output policy projections.

scenarios.name: architecture-017

scenarios.then: one authority serializes the transaction

requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: the native family policy determines focus and hit order; failure injection and artifact hashes included.

scenarios.name: architecture-018
scenarios.given: a draft modal overlaps a maximized window
scenarios.when: a user clicks a visible native region
scenarios.then: the native family policy determines focus and hit order

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL transport preview identifiers and revisions through ports while native components retain pixel buffers and verify source-stop lifetime.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: the valid retained frame remains available without JSON pixels; failure injection and artifact hashes included.

scenarios.then: the valid retained frame remains available without JSON pixels

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL distinguish native effect receipts from native frame-presentation receipts and keep motion sampling and buffer retirement under native ownership.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: presentation is unproven until the native receipt; failure injection and artifact hashes included.
requirements.task: Expose separate commit and presentation evidence.

scenarios.name: architecture-020
scenarios.given: a motion effect accepted by authority
scenarios.then: presentation is unproven until the native receipt

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL compare GTK/WebKitGTK and a dedicated Qt/WebEngine host using the same Elm assets, compositor tuple, workload and measurement definitions.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: separate native results and resource measurements are retained; failure injection and artifact hashes included.

scenarios.name: architecture-021
scenarios.when: the same vertical slice is tested
scenarios.then: separate native results and resource measurements are retained

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL create native layer and popup roles, input regions and keyboard-interactivity settings before exposing their Elm views.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: roles and input masks precede frontend readiness; failure injection and artifact hashes included.

scenarios.then: roles and input masks precede frontend readiness

scenarios.name: architecture-023
scenarios.then: each named route has native evidence or blocks release

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL load packaged shell assets from an allowlisted local origin and deny remote navigation, arbitrary native method invocation and unapproved resource URLs.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: navigation or capability access is denied; failure injection and artifact hashes included.

scenarios.then: navigation or capability access is denied

requirements.ears: IF a compositor plugin does not match its recorded owning compositor ABI tuple, THEN the Elm desktop SHALL refuse plugin loading.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: the plugin is not loaded and the mismatch is reported; failure injection and artifact hashes included.

scenarios.name: architecture-025
scenarios.then: the plugin is not loaded and the mismatch is reported

requirements.ears: WHEN the frontend or renderer restarts, the Elm desktop SHALL invalidate its old epoch, revoke its owned resources and reconcile a fresh snapshot before admitting new effects.
requirements.verification: Preserved scenario report with native or bridge trace showing: old work is refused and effects await snapshot reconciliation; failure injection and artifact hashes included.

scenarios.then: old work is refused and effects await snapshot reconciliation

requirements.ears: WHEN Elm shell activation fails its release checks, the Elm desktop SHALL restore the recorded accepted shell configuration without restarting the compositor or closing application windows.

scenarios.given: the accepted shell configuration is saved
scenarios.then: the accepted shell returns and drafts remain connected

requirements.task: Implement and validate the separately approved native compositor backend.

scenarios.then: nested and hardware evidence precedes main-session use

scenarios.then: WebGPU and displayed-render verdicts remain unproven until their probes pass

requirements.ears: WHEN WebGPU is evaluated, the native host SHALL expose bundled assets through a qualified secure local origin without disabling renderer sandboxing.
requirements.verification: Origin/security-state probe, effective sandbox flags and denied remote navigation.

scenarios.name: gpu-003
scenarios.when: the host loads its GPU probe

requirements.ears: WHEN a WebGPU adapter or device is unavailable, the host SHALL reject WebGPU qualification and preserve an accepted alternative hardware-rendering route.
requirements.verification: Null-adapter, rejected-device and unsupported-feature fault reports.
requirements.task: Implement capability negotiation and API rejection.

scenarios.name: gpu-004
scenarios.given: an accepted native GPU path and a WebGPU probe
scenarios.then: WebGPU is unqualified while the native GPU path remains usable

requirements.ears: The WebGPU qualification SHALL verify a deterministic render and compute result using supported adapter limits and features and independently observe the native displayed frame.
requirements.verification: WGSL validation/readback results plus output capture and backend classification.
requirements.task: Build isolated render and compute qualification probes.

scenarios.name: gpu-005
scenarios.given: a nonsoftware adapter and accepted device
scenarios.then: known results match and the rendered native frame is independently observed

requirements.ears: WHILE GPU effects are active, the renderer SHALL own GPU objects locally and keep per-frame pixel buffers outside Elm port messages.
requirements.verification: IPC payload and resource-allocation traces over motion/reversal workload.
requirements.task: Keep GPU ownership and frame scheduling in the renderer.

scenarios.name: gpu-006

scenarios.then: ports carry bounded control metadata and GPU objects remain renderer-owned

requirements.verification: Device-loss injection and generation/effect logs with no stale native mutation.
requirements.task: Implement bounded device-loss recovery.

scenarios.name: gpu-007
scenarios.given: GPU resources and an old pending window intent
scenarios.then: old resources become unusable and the old intent is not automatically committed

requirements.ears: The preview qualification SHALL measure actual native-buffer import, synchronization and copy volume instead of inferring zero-copy support from WebGPU availability.
requirements.verification: Native fence/import trace and copy bytes/counts on both GPU configurations.
requirements.task: Qualify the preview interoperability path.

scenarios.name: gpu-008
scenarios.given: a native frame lease and a WebGPU-capable host
scenarios.then: the report records actual copies and fences without claiming an untested DMA-BUF import

requirements.ears: IF every qualified GPU path becomes unavailable, THEN the host SHALL expose essential recovery controls in a disclosed degraded mode and block accelerated release admission.
requirements.verification: All-backend-failure fault plus offline recovery/qualification report.
requirements.task: Qualify degraded recovery and release refusal.

scenarios.name: gpu-009
scenarios.then: essential controls remain accessible and the report identifies software/degraded execution

requirements.ears: The GPU qualification SHALL compare integrated and discrete execution, where selectable, against frozen latency, memory, power and transfer budgets on the actual output configuration.
requirements.verification: Hardware profile manifest and controlled sample distributions including cross-GPU transfers.

scenarios.name: gpu-010
scenarios.given: Intel and NVIDIA devices in the inventory
scenarios.then: each profile identifies the actual device and measured workload verdict

scenarios.when: the user clicks the unrelated eligible window
scenarios.then: native policy focuses the intended eligible recipient without closing drafts

requirements.ears: WHEN an output scale, transform or generation changes, the native renderer SHALL invalidate incompatible frame geometry and rebuild presentation against current output truth.
requirements.verification: Mixed-scale native screenshots and receipts confirm geometry revision changes.
requirements.task: Handle fractional scale, negative coordinates, rotation and hotplug.

scenarios.name: ren-019
scenarios.then: stale output geometry is rejected and current pixels align

requirements.ears: WHEN a window transfers between outputs, the canonical authority SHALL commit placement, snap membership and frame ownership using current output generations.
requirements.verification: Transfer/hotplug race packet records one committed owner and correct geometry.
requirements.task: Serialize transfer and cancellation with output removal and snap policy.

scenarios.name: ren-020
scenarios.then: the stale target is refused and ownership reconciles

requirements.ears: WHERE 240 Hz hardware is available, WHILE motion is active, the native renderer SHALL sample motion in its native presentation loop and record cadence against a same-machine baseline.
requirements.verification: 240 Hz hardware packet records frame gaps, latency quantiles and hardware configuration.
requirements.task: Benchmark native motion without per-frame Elm JSON; set budgets from baseline.

scenarios.name: ren-021
scenarios.given: documented 240 Hz hardware and baseline exist
scenarios.then: native cadence measurements and comparative budgets are published

requirements.ears: The release gate SHALL distinguish renderer receipts from independent presentation evidence and report latency, memory, wakeups and resource growth against the chosen host baseline.
requirements.verification: Comparison packet separates unsupported GPU/presentation spans and measured metrics.
requirements.task: Instrument both host candidates and document observer overhead and missing stages.

scenarios.name: ren-022
scenarios.then: queue receipts are not counted as displayed-frame proof

requirements.ears: WHERE a compositor replacement is selected, the project SHALL document a native Rust or C++ execution boundary and an Elm policy interface before implementation.
requirements.verification: Reviewed feasibility decision records staffing, excluded scope and native authority.
requirements.task: Choose native framework after protocol, license, backend and maintenance evaluation.

scenarios.name: ren-023
scenarios.given: replacement remains an optional product goal
scenarios.then: the plan names native ownership rather than promising pure Elm

requirements.ears: WHERE compositor replacement is selected, the native compositor SHALL implement a versioned Wayland and Xwayland compatibility matrix with explicit unsupported cases.
requirements.verification: Nested client matrix covers Brave, GTK, Qt and X11 lifecycle and modality.
requirements.task: Implement xdg roles, configure/ack lifecycle and legacy X11 focus/window management.

scenarios.name: ren-024
scenarios.given: Wayland and X11 clients share the session
scenarios.then: supported semantics pass and unsupported cases are reported

requirements.ears: WHERE compositor replacement is selected, the native compositor SHALL own DRM/KMS outputs, seat input and session transitions independently of Elm responsiveness.
requirements.verification: Hardware campaign logs modes, input, suspend/resume and hotplug recovery.
requirements.task: Implement hotplug, modes, leases, suspend/resume and input-device lifecycle.

scenarios.name: ren-025
scenarios.then: native seat and output handling remain responsive

requirements.ears: WHERE compositor replacement is selected, the native compositor SHALL provide tested IME, preedit and text-input integration for its supported application matrix.
requirements.verification: Native multilingual preedit/commit tests cover GTK, Qt, browser and Xwayland support.
requirements.task: Implement native text-input/input-method routes with focus and security isolation.

scenarios.name: ren-026
scenarios.given: a supported app has an active preedit
scenarios.then: text and focus follow the documented IME lifecycle

requirements.ears: WHERE compositor replacement is selected, the native compositor SHALL gate capture and remote-control access through documented portal and permission boundaries.
requirements.verification: Consent, denial, revocation and cross-session capture tests record no unauthorized frames.
requirements.task: Integrate screencopy/PipeWire portal paths, revocation and session isolation.

scenarios.name: ren-027
scenarios.then: new capture and remote-input access stop

requirements.ears: WHERE compositor replacement is selected, the native compositor SHALL validate client requests and isolate privileged protocols from untrusted shell content.
requirements.verification: Malformed-client fuzzing and lock/input/capture isolation results identify residual risks.
requirements.task: Threat-model IPC, protocol exposure, buffer parsing, lock surfaces and client isolation.

scenarios.name: ren-028
scenarios.given: an untrusted client sends malformed protocol traffic
scenarios.then: privileged operations remain denied and other clients remain isolated

requirements.ears: WHERE compositor replacement is selected, the native compositor SHALL retain frame scheduling, fences, hit testing and buffer retirement in native loops without awaiting Elm port replies.
requirements.verification: Injected frontend stalls preserve native frame/input progress and bounded ownership.
requirements.task: Implement asynchronous policy snapshots and bounded native policy fallback.

scenarios.name: ren-029
scenarios.given: Elm is paused or its webview crashes
scenarios.then: native loops continue under the documented fallback policy

requirements.ears: WHERE compositor replacement is selected, the deployment plan SHALL provide tested session fallback and recovery instructions that disclose loss of application connections on compositor failure.
requirements.verification: Recovery drill logs shell-only restart separately from compositor crash and fallback login.
requirements.task: Stage nested then sacrificial hardware sessions; preserve user drafts before cutover.

scenarios.name: ren-030
scenarios.given: the optional compositor fails in a sacrificial session
scenarios.then: a working fallback session starts with connection-loss limits documented

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL maintain a scope inventory that assigns each shell surface a migration owner, acceptance scenario and rollback destination.
requirements.verification: Review signed inventory against source paths; no unassigned surface.
requirements.task: Inventory taskbar, launcher, switcher, Task View, snap, menus, settings, notifications and Files integration.

scenarios.name: ux-001
scenarios.then: every inventoried surface has an owner, scenario and rollback route

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL place taskbar application icons at the left edge of each configured taskbar output.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: first icon begins at the configured left inset on each output.
requirements.task: Implement left anchored taskbar layout with scale-aware reserved work area.

scenarios.name: ux-002
scenarios.then: first icon begins at the configured left inset on each output

requirements.ears: WHEN the desktop catalog changes, the Elm desktop SHALL refresh application entries using desktop-file visibility and launch semantics.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: only eligible entries appear and launches preserve recorded arguments.

scenarios.name: ux-003
scenarios.then: only eligible entries appear and launches preserve recorded arguments

requirements.ears: WHEN a user reorders or pins an application icon, the Elm desktop SHALL persist its desktop identity and relative order across shell restart.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: both identities retain the chosen relative order.

scenarios.name: ux-004
scenarios.then: both identities retain the chosen relative order

requirements.ears: WHEN a taskbar group is opened, the Elm desktop SHALL list each eligible window incarnation once and route selection to that incarnation.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: three entries appear and only selected incarnation receives activation.
requirements.task: Implement window grouping and native validated selection.

scenarios.name: ux-005
scenarios.when: group is opened and one member selected
scenarios.then: three entries appear and only selected incarnation receives activation

requirements.ears: WHILE a window is minimized, the Elm desktop SHALL retain its taskbar identity and label its retained preview as historical.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: entry remains present with historical preview label.
requirements.task: Represent minimized entries and retained preview freshness separately.

scenarios.name: ux-006
scenarios.then: entry remains present with historical preview label

requirements.ears: WHEN a retained preview is unavailable, the Elm desktop SHALL display the application icon and window title without substituting another incarnation’s pixels.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: fallback shows correct title and icon with no unrelated pixels.
requirements.task: Add explicit unavailable-preview view and lifetime-key validation.

scenarios.name: ux-007
scenarios.then: fallback shows correct title and icon with no unrelated pixels

requirements.ears: WHEN an eligible taskbar window is selected, the Elm desktop SHALL request activation or restore through native authority without moving it to a scratchpad.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: native receipt confirms restore and workspace membership has not become scratchpad.
requirements.task: Port click-to-activate and restore intent path.

scenarios.name: ux-008
scenarios.then: native receipt confirms restore and workspace membership has not become scratchpad

requirements.ears: WHILE native observations mark a window active or attention-requesting, the Elm desktop SHALL expose distinct active and attention indicators.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: attention indicator differs from active indicator in pixels and accessible state.
requirements.task: Derive highlights from native observations rather than optimistic clicks.

scenarios.name: ux-009
scenarios.then: attention indicator differs from active indicator in pixels and accessible state

requirements.ears: WHEN a user invokes an application jump list, the Elm desktop SHALL show only catalog-declared actions and supported recent-item actions for that application identity.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: two declared actions appear and unsupported actions are absent.

scenarios.name: ux-010
scenarios.then: two declared actions appear and unsupported actions are absent

requirements.ears: WHEN native Alt-Tab chord events arrive, the Elm desktop SHALL advance selection in the frozen eligible-window order for that chord generation.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: selection advances then returns within the same frozen order.

scenarios.name: ux-011
scenarios.then: selection advances then returns within the same frozen order

requirements.ears: WHEN Alt release precedes switcher readiness, the Elm desktop SHALL resolve the native chord once without leaving an open switcher or issuing a second activation.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: one resolution occurs and no switcher remains open.
requirements.task: Preserve native pre-ready key journal and single commit guard.

scenarios.name: ux-012
scenarios.when: Alt press, Tab and release precede readiness
scenarios.then: one resolution occurs and no switcher remains open

requirements.ears: WHEN Escape cancels a switcher chord before native commit, the Elm desktop SHALL close the switcher and preserve the previously focused window.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: switcher closes and focus is unchanged.
requirements.task: Implement native cancellation boundary and focus-preservation replay.

scenarios.name: ux-013
scenarios.given: switcher selection differs from focused window
scenarios.then: switcher closes and focus is unchanged

requirements.ears: IF the selected switcher window closes or its identity becomes stale, THEN the Elm desktop SHALL reselect a surviving eligible member or dismiss an empty chord without activating a replacement incarnation.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: reused address is never activated as the closed window.
requirements.task: Handle close and incarnation reuse during chord.

scenarios.name: ux-014
scenarios.given: selected window closes and address is reused
scenarios.then: reused address is never activated as the closed window

requirements.ears: WHEN a user activates a modal family, the Elm desktop SHALL request the native eligible modal target while preserving the application’s draft content.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: native modal target or terminal activates and draft content remains intact.
requirements.task: Use native family relations and prohibit shell draft reconstruction.

scenarios.name: ux-015
scenarios.given: Brave draft dialog and unrelated terminal overlap
scenarios.then: native modal target or terminal activates and draft content remains intact

requirements.ears: WHEN a user toggles always-on-top on a maximized family, the Elm desktop SHALL display pin and maximize state only after correlated native observations.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: displayed pin/MAX state agrees with native state and visible hit target.
requirements.task: Implement pin/MAX intent state with committed-state presentation.

scenarios.name: ux-016
scenarios.then: displayed pin/MAX state agrees with native state and visible hit target

requirements.ears: WHEN Task View opens, the Elm desktop SHALL show eligible windows grouped by workspace with a keyboard-selectable active-workspace marker.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: groups match native membership and active workspace is named.
requirements.task: Build Task View from canonical workspace/window projection.

scenarios.name: ux-017
scenarios.then: groups match native membership and active workspace is named

requirements.ears: WHEN a user transfers a window through Task View, the Elm desktop SHALL update workspace membership only after native transfer acceptance.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: accepted transfer updates membership; refusal retains workspace 1.
requirements.task: Implement transfer transaction and refused-state feedback.

scenarios.name: ux-018
scenarios.then: accepted transfer updates membership; refusal retains workspace 1

requirements.ears: WHEN a user chooses a snap region, the Elm desktop SHALL submit geometry keyed to the selected output generation and show the accepted native placement.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: accepted placement matches half work area within native rounding tolerance.
requirements.task: Implement snap chooser and native placement reconciliation.

scenarios.name: ux-019
scenarios.given: output has a defined work area
scenarios.then: accepted placement matches half work area within native rounding tolerance

requirements.ears: IF an output changes during snap selection, THEN the Elm desktop SHALL invalidate the old preview and require geometry derived from the new output generation before commit.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: old generation geometry is never committed.
requirements.task: Invalidate snap transactions on scale, transform and hotplug changes.

scenarios.name: ux-020
scenarios.when: output scale changes or output disappears
scenarios.then: old generation geometry is never committed

requirements.ears: WHEN a user drags or resizes an application window, the Elm desktop SHALL preserve native pointer ownership until release or explicit cancellation.

scenarios.given: drag crosses the taskbar and another output
scenarios.then: exactly one gesture ends and no shell surface steals the drag

requirements.ears: WHILE reduced motion is enabled, the Elm desktop SHALL use the documented reduced-motion transition profile for minimize, restore and shell overlays.
requirements.verification: Elm replay assertion and isolated native recording: recorded transitions match approved reduced-motion profile.

scenarios.name: ux-022
scenarios.then: recorded transitions match approved reduced-motion profile

requirements.ears: The Elm desktop SHALL provide keyboard routes for launcher, taskbar groups, switcher, Task View, snap chooser, menus and settings without requiring pointer input.

scenarios.then: each surface can be opened, operated and dismissed without pointer events

scenarios.then: labels and focus remain visible and every action retains a hit target

scenarios.then: one request occurs and refused launch displays an error
